Orlazam-az-Dihr (I04)

Scoring-table region: Serpentspine.

In one sentence: reconnect the lost ram hold, pastures, and forges, then let dwarves ride mechanical rams to turn the mountains into a cavalry state.

Story: high | Mission-tree length: long (36 direct I04 missions) | Mission-tree update: dedicated tree in the current local version | Uniqueness: very high | Grind: medium | Early pressure: medium-high | Expansion ability: above average.

Identity and history

Orlazam-az-Dihr is a Ramsteel Dwarf country in the western Serpentspine, Tag I04. It is not a native 1444 country: it is formed by a Dwarven Adventurer company after reclaiming Hold 4147 and meeting the administrative technology and mountain-recovery requirements through the Dwarven formation decision. The current Chinese localisation gives I04 a Chinese display name; this English layer uses the native Mod name Orlazam-az-dihr.

The offline Wiki calls it the Hold of Orlazam-az-dihr and places it among the western dwarves. Ramsteel is not ordinary steel: trained rams strike the metal while it cools, rapidly hardening it. The hold’s identity therefore connects pastoralism, cavalry, mining, and smithing rather than being merely another mining hold. This related Wiki material supplements the setting and does not establish current mechanics.

National story and campaign arc

I04’s mission tree begins with restoring the old flocks. Early missions ask the player to develop the Logr frontier, restore sheep pens, and make the first charge with at least ten cavalry. The national fantasy is therefore expressed through provincial development, livestock management, and a gradual cavalry build-up rather than free mechanical cavalry at game start.

The middle game is about recovering valleys, farms, and plains: repairing irrigation, reclaiming ancestral land, developing pastures, extending production facilities and grasslands through the northern passage, and pushing into the Moitsa plains. A parallel branch reclaims Ramvault, restores forges and mines, rediscovers the secrets of Ramsteel, and joins iron, mithril, and smithing facilities to the national production chain.

The end state is not simply the conquest of every dwarf. One direction rebuilds the hold’s industry through mines, weapons research, and the Frostforge; the other advances animal training, runic horns, mithril armour, firearms training, and the mechanical-ram prototype. The final rewards depend on investment in money, technology, armies, and artificer support. This is a production–research–cavalry loop, not ordinary military bonuses with a different label.

Core mechanics

The signature mechanic is the staged upgrade of Ramsteel cavalry. The first charge needs cavalry-ratio and unit-number thresholds. Later missions require military technology or innovativeness, a military reformer, mithril weapons, artificer loyalty, and substantial funds. The mechanical-ram prototype costs 1,000 ducats; if artificer loyalty is insufficient, three categories of monarch points are used instead. It is not a free permanent unit.

The second loop is hold production. Pasture missions turn provinces toward wool or livestock; mining missions require several iron provinces to have production buildings and increased output; after mithril is secured, the chain connects mithril and forges to Ramsteel production. Expansion and economic development are consequently locked together: fighting without improving mines, pastures, or workshops can block the cavalry later.

The third loop is the transition from adventurer company to hold country. The formation decision requires the core of Hold 4147, a Dwarven administrative reform, administrative technology 7, peace, and at least three cities. On formation, I04 changes to Ramsteel culture, fixes its capital, and replaces non-generic missions. These are formation requirements, not 1444 starting capabilities.

Phased play

At the start, arrange the target hold and nearby colonisation, expeditions, and hold restoration, aiming to meet the formation conditions without spending every administrative point on unrelated conquest. After forming I04, complete the sheep pens, first charge, and irrigation branch, establish a stable livestock and wool economy, and then push into the grasslands and plains.

In the middle game, connect Ramvault, iron, and production buildings, then choose whether the ram-cavalry line should favour shock or fire. The missions contain script effects that replace shock and fire modifiers; the choice changes the army’s feel. Community reports treat shock as the more natural cavalry route and fire as more dependent on later firearms and artificer stacking. This is community experience, not current numeric proof.

Late game revolves around mithril armour, mechanical rams, the Frostforge, and further hold expansion. The tree links cavalry, production, colonisation, and Dwarven mountain recovery, but Adventurer colonisation, disasters, and manpower pressure remain. A powerful endgame does not imply an easy opening.

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 78/100 | Authoritarianism 55/100 | Magic–Artifice 20/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 76/100) | Pluralism 45/100.

The v2.1 values classification is Neutral (63/100), with a stable trajectory.

The explanatory v2.1 profile is Expansion 78 | Authoritarianism 55 | Magic direction 20 (theme intensity 76) | Pluralism 45. Its magic-direction coordinate points towards artifice: forging, engineering, mechanical rams and artificers, rather than a powerful mage-state, define the campaign. The high intensity reflects these systems' importance to the mission endgame. [Local scripts]

The v2.1 value assessment is neutral (63/100) with a stable trajectory. The dimensions are dignity 64, public good 72, personhood 58, and restraint 52; weighted at 35%, 25%, 25%, and 15%, respectively, the result rounds to 63. Missions invest in pastures, irrigation, cities, mines, and public defence, supporting a strong public-good reading. The available material says little about population policy or treatment of residents. War, armaments, Dwarven identity, expansion, and state formation are not by themselves deductions; no concrete systemic enslavement or population-as-resource harm is currently confirmed.

This country suits players who enjoy growing one unusual unit into a major force while managing colonisation, mining, and finances. Avoid it if you want pure infantry, pure diplomacy, or no Dwarven disaster and mountain-development management.

Community experience and evidence boundaries

Two player discussions describe the core experience as “dwarves riding mechanical rams”: one emphasises late-game mechanical rams and high shock, while another discusses the shock/fire branch and cavalry ratio. They support play-feel only and do not establish current mission rewards or values. The original research did not establish a dedicated official I04 development diary with readable body text. It also recorded inaccessible Halann historical-map research and reference pages, which were not adopted. This text-only translation does not repeat those online investigations. See the evidence page for complete source paths, line ranges, Wiki metadata, Reddit counts, and unresolved gaps.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces native English national-idea names and descriptions alongside the inherited source displays. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Successor ideas do not stack automatically with the predecessor set. Descriptions may recount history or depict a future ideal, not events already completed in 1444. Native English prose is used rather than back-translating the Chinese localisation; any inherited display/unit uncertainty remains unresolved.

Orlazam-az-dihr (I04) — Ramsteel Ideas

Traditions: Ramsteel Traditions

Effects: Army Tradition from battles: +1; Reinforce cost: -15%.

Idea 1: Originator of Ram Cavalry

The renowned chargers of dwarven ram cavalry in fact originated in Orlazam-az-dihr. The first ram rangers started life as frontier woodsmen and farmers who later formed a close bond with the native rams - it is said that a bond between an Ramsteel and their mount was stronger than that with their spouse!

Effects: Cavalry combat ability: +20%; Cavalry ratio: +25%.

Idea 2: Stewards of Vale and Beyond

During the days of Aul-Dwarov the Ramsteels were tasked with protecting the terraced farms of the Serpent's Vale against any would-be intruder from beyond, from early human tribes to trolls and ogres.

Effects: Movement speed: +15%.

Idea 3: Ramsteel Battering Process

Before the age of Kronium, Adamantium and Mithril, there was Ramsteel. This steel was first forged by the ancient proto-dwarves who trained their rams to hit heated sheets of metal in order to harden it more than any ordinary dwarf could. Known for its hardness and durability, Ramsteel would go on to be the favoured metal for many warriors.

Effects: Production efficiency: +10%.

Idea 4: The Charge of Tednur Fourfoot

The greatest of the Ramlords of Orlazam was Tednur Fourfoot, who famously led a devastating cavalry charge against one of the largest goblin hordes in history. Records say the cavalry's wake was so devastating that the infantry following kept slipping and sliding on the mashed and slushed innards of goblins.

Effects: Leader land manoeuvre: +1; Shock damage: +5%.

Idea 5: Legend of the Slow-roasted Orlazam Lamb

By the time Aul-Dwarov was founded the days of ramsteel dominance were long over and many dwarves focused and cultivated their mastery of meats and cattle. The Orlazam Lamb became a staple in the halls of dwarven kings, known for its juicy meats and sun-kissed flavours from the surface that were exotic to Orlazam's more underground-dwelling kin.

Effects: Diplomatic reputation: +200%.

Idea 6: Hornwall Execution

An infamous practice of the Ramlords against disobedient subjects was the Hornwall Punishment, which involved lining up the offending dwarves against the wall and having rams smash into them.

Effects: National unrest: -1; Harsh treatment cost: -20%.

Idea 7: Unwavering Loyalty

Loyalty to the High King was commonplace among the Ramsteel Dwarf Clans, as their cooperation with the neighbouring hold of Amldihr had brought prosperity for the nobles and ram herders. The two holds fostered very friendly relations with each other, often siding with each other in Amlharaz debates and other disputes. Land rights to the vale were granted for herds, many privileges for the hold and nobles were granted, and favouritism was practised due to Ramsteel loyalty. The Ram Riders fought to the end to aid the last High King against the orcs besieging in King’s Rock, even while having lost, they proved their loyalty to be unwavering.

Effects: War exhaustion: -0.03.

Ambition: Ramsteel Ambition

Effects: Leader land shock: +1.
